title: How can angles turned different ways be compared?
description: Four angles with different openings point in different directions. Each angle is labelled with the vertex as the middle letter, one is traced, and the trace is laid over another with the vertices together. Keeko's doubt is that the angle which looks biggest must be the biggest.
teaching_notes: One idea: label each angle, then compare by laying one over another with the vertices together and one arm along one arm. Watch for students who pick the angle that merely looks biggest.

source: Here are some angles (four angles drawn with different openi
video_script.why: The child learns to label angles and to compare two angles by superimposition.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four angles with different openings and directions
video_script.anchor: the four angles of the book, drawn with different openings and directions
video_script.wrong_answer: the angle that looks biggest is the biggest
video_script.wrong_move: compares angles by eye when they point in different directions
video_script.payoff_line: Label each angle, then superimpose to compare

final_answer.value: label each angle; compare by superimposition
final_answer.spoken: label each angle with its vertex in the middle, then lay one over another with the vertices together

maths_rules: label each angle with a point on each arm and the vertex as the middle letter
trace one angle on thin paper
lay the traced angle on another with the vertices together and one arm along one arm
if the other arm of the traced angle falls inside, the traced angle is smaller; if it falls outside, it is larger; if it falls on the arm, they are equal
slip: an angle that looks biggest may not be the biggest when the angles point in different directions
video_script.design: One idea: label, then compare by superimposition. The four angles of the book stay on the board all video. Keeko's doubt: the one that looks biggest is the biggest.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four angles drawn with different openings, turned in different directions

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.angles: the four angles appear, each turned a different way
marks.ask: a question mark rises over the angles

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about angles.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>Here are four angles. They have different openings, and they point in different directions.

beats.on_screen: the four angles stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one traced angle laid over another angle with the vertices together

marks.lay: a traced angle slides over a second angle
marks.vertex: the two vertices meet and glow

narration: <bookmark mark='lay'/>Placing one angle over another is called superimposition.
<bookmark mark='vertex'/>While doing it, the vertices of the two angles must overlap.

beats.on_screen: Given: four angles with different openings and directions
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four angles with different openings, pointing in different directions.

beats.on_screen: To find: a label for each angle, and a way to compare them

marks.find: the words label and compare are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to label each angle and find a way to compare them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: label each angle, a point on each arm and the vertex in the middle

marks.label: a letter is written on the vertex and on a point of each arm of every angle

narration: <bookmark mark='label'/>Step one, label each angle. Write a letter on a point of each arm, and write the vertex letter in the middle.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: trace one angle on thin paper

marks.trace: one angle is copied onto thin paper

narration: <bookmark mark='trace'/>Step two, trace one angle on thin paper, because we cannot lift a drawn angle off the page.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: lay the traced angle on another, vertices together, one arm along one arm

marks.lay: the trace slides onto another angle, the vertices meet and one pair of arms lines up

narration: <bookmark mark='lay'/>Step three, lay the traced angle on another angle. The vertices must overlap, and one arm must lie along one arm.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: look at the other arm; inside means smaller, outside means larger

marks.inside: the second arm of the trace is seen inside the other angle
marks.outside: the second arm of the trace is seen outside the other angle

narration: <bookmark mark='inside'/>Step four, look at where the other arm of the trace falls. If it falls inside the other angle, the traced angle is smaller.
<bookmark mark='outside'/>If it falls outside, the traced angle is larger.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Label each angle, then superimpose to compare
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Label each angle, then superimpose to compare.
Any two of the four angles can be compared in this way.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: two angles turned different ways look different in size; the traced copy laid on them shows the truth

marks.doubt: the angle that looks biggest is circled
marks.fix: the traced copy is laid on both angles
marks.fair: the two arms line up and the circle moves

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the angle that looks biggest is the biggest.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But when angles point in different directions, our eyes can be fooled.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>Laying one on another is a fair test. It does not depend on how the angles are turned.
